title: Batch formation freeze during peak — incident review and mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Ramos
description: Summary: On 2025-11-02 and again on 2025-11-03 we observed multiple 10–30s tail latency spikes caused by complete batch formation stalls in the continuous batching layer. The behavior manifested under high concurrent request rates to the hosted API: a subset of serving workers stopped emitting completed batches for several seconds, which caused request queues to accumulate and customer requests to either time out or fall back to slower model variants. This ticket consolidates the incident timeline, root-cause analysis, and a prioritized set of mitigations with owners and deadlines.
impact_summary: Affected hosted customers experienced elevated 95/99th token latency and occasional request timeouts during peak bursts in EU and us-west regions. Estimated user-facing error rate increased by ~0.6% across our tenant population for the two incident windows; a handful of high-throughput customers saw sustained throughput degradation for up to 7 minutes. No data loss, but SLA targets were missed for impacted windows.
timeline_summary:
2025-11-02 14:07 UTC: First small spike observed; automated alert fired (tail-latency > 3s).
2025-11-02 14:12 UTC: On-call routed to continuous-batcher team.
2025-11-02 14:18 UTC: Temporary mitigation (scale-up dedicated workers) reduced impact; root cause unknown.
2025-11-03 09:40 UTC: Repeat and larger incident; batch formation on some workers halted for 8–26s.
2025-11-03 09:46 UTC: Rollback of a recent kernel-selection change reverted on canary; partial recovery observed.
2025-11-03 10:10 UTC: Hotfix deployed to runtime to force batch window reset on worker start; incident resolved.
2025-11-04: Begin forensic logs and artifact collection; reproduce attempts started on staging with synthetic traffic.
root_cause: Combined regression: an interaction between the new epoch-based batching window (rolled in runtime-1.22) and a rare KV cache eviction pattern. During specific token length distribution bursts, the batch window state machine failed to advance when an internal rate-limiter reported zero available slots due to transient kernel selection backpressure. The result was 'batch formation freeze' where the worker's batch queue did not emit for multiple seconds. Race conditions in the window-reset path meant that the usual watchdog did not always trigger, explaining why the freeze duration varied.
mitigations: Immediate actions taken: scaled worker pool in impacted regions; reverted canary kernel-selection change; deployed hotfix to explicitly reset batch window on kernel thrash detection. Longer-term mitigations proposed below.
action_items: A1: Add deterministic unit + chaos tests for epoch-window transitions (owner: Noor Patel) — due 2025-11-17
A2: Implement a configurable watchdog to enforce max batch formation latency per worker and emit telemetry when reset occurs (owner: Liam Chen) — due 2025-11-24
A3: Add a fallback path that bypasses epoch batching to a legacy coalescer for 200ms if prolonged non-emission is detected (owner: Marco Silva) — due 2025-12-01
A4: Improve observability: export per-worker batch-window state, rate-limiter backpressure counters, and KV-eviction events to Grafana (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2025-11-14
A5: Roll forward stricter pre-merge perf tests for kernel-selection changes gated by synthetic long-tail traffic profiles (owner: Jonas Becker) — due 2025-11-21
A6: Run canary in a small fleet configured with tighter batch watchdogs for 2 weeks before wide rollout (owner: Liam Chen) — due 2025-12-08
A7: Customer communications: draft post-incident summary and offer technical review to top-affected accounts (owner: Aisha Ramos) — due 2025-11-12
comments: 2025-11-04 17:20 UTC — Noor Patel: Reproduced batch freeze locally with a crafted token-length distribution and KV-eviction throttle. Adding deterministic seed to reproduce intermittency.
2025-11-05 09:02 UTC — Liam Chen: Hotfix validated on canary for 36 hours with no recurrence; preparing rollout checklist. Will add telemetry MTTI (mean time to intervention).

2025-11-06 15:44 UTC — Priya Nair: Grafana panels added for per-worker state. Early dashboards show several workers in eu-west exhibiting high rate-limiter stall counters prior to non-emission events.
2025-11-08 12:11 UTC — Marco Silva: Prototype fallback coalescer achieves 70% reduction in observed tail when injected on staging with synthetic bursts. Needs safety tests before production flip.
